source: Community surveys · GTAForums spending analysis · estimated from DLC category releases · Lehdonvirta (2014) virtual economy framework
note: Spending distribution across GTA$ expenditure categories per major era. Figures are community-estimated; Rockstar does not publish aggregate spending breakdowns. Classified as 'modelled' data.

categories.label: Vehicles
categories.note: Cars, bikes, aircraft, boats, combat vehicles. Single largest category.

categories.label: Properties / Biz
categories.note: Garages, apartments, businesses (Bunker, Nightclub, Acid Lab etc.), MC businesses.

categories.label: Weapons / Mods
categories.note: Weapons, upgrades, vehicle mods, armour, ammo. Recurring session cost.

categories.label: Shark Card equivalents
categories.note: Proxy: share of spending on high-value single items (Shark Card-funded purchases).

eras.label: 2013–14 Launch
eras.note: Properties mostly apartments — no business ecosystem yet. Vehicles dominated.

eras.label: 2015 Heists
eras.note: Heist players accumulate faster; some shift to property accumulation.

eras.label: 2016–17 Biz Era
eras.note: Passive income businesses (Bunker, MC) absorb large share of GTA$. Property investment spike.

eras.label: 2018 After Hours
eras.note: Oppressor Mk II at $3.9M drives vehicle spending up sharply. Single item dominates sales.

eras.label: 2019–20 Casino Era
eras.note: Penthouse + casino suite add premium property tier. Vehicle/property close to parity.

eras.label: 2021–22 Cayo Era
eras.note: High yield lets players buy consumables freely. Weapons/mods spending rises. Reference screenshot era.

eras.label: 2023–25 Current
eras.note: Chop Shop vehicles add new mid-tier aspirational cars. Modest property share recovery.
